clue.text: The odd pie calls for added seasoning

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a strange pie needs extra spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the letters of PIE CALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice from the berries of a West Indian tree, used to season food.

clue.text: Not now to be seen in a Southern Hellenic city

indicators.note: one word is found sitting inside the others, so this phrase signals a container

parts.note: something done not now was done then

explanation.surface: Something no longer visible in a Greek city of the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be seen in' puts THEN inside A plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Greece, a city whose people are Hellenes.

clue.text: Bring down to earth over gold 16

parts.note: to land an aircraft is to bring it down to earth
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone is deflated over their gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' points to the answer to 16 down, CARRIAGE, which is the definition here; 'over' places LAND first in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding top, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Heartless people lay a little money

indicators.note: taking away the heart leaves only the first and last letters of the word people

parts.note: to lay something down is to set it

explanation.surface: Cruel folk put down a few coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The peseta was the Spanish currency before the euro; a single one was worth very little.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Spanish coin of small value, so a modest sum.

clue.text: Appear in need, but not so — funny woman!

parts.note: to come is to appear or arrive

indicators.note: not so says the letters are not arranged so, meaning they must be reordered

explanation.surface: A comic plays poor but is not really poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' rearranges IN NEED into DIENNE, added after COME.
explanation.definitionFit: A female comic performer, the feminine form of comedian.

clue.text: Becoming a supporter with evident hesitation

parts.note: a prop is a support holding something up
er is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a backer, though plainly unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' is an adjective here, meaning fitting or seemly, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean suitable and decorous, as in seemly behaviour.

clue.text: A writer offering serving men a drink

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers serving in the British Army
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A writer buys a round for the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER is a dark British beer, once popular with market porters.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who writes news stories.

clue.text: Irregular worker after small change

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other, so the worker follows the small change

parts.note: p stands for a penny, a small coin
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A casual labourer chases loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' is a noun: an irregular soldier, a guerrilla fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a guerrilla fighter, a member of irregular armed forces.

clue.text: Salad food prepared by an artistic person?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
dishes are items of food made ready to eat

explanation.surface: A painter makes up a plate of salad.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for a Royal Academician, an artist elected to London's Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Small red roots usually eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Pass several, being liberal

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it over
some means a number of, several

explanation.surface: Someone hands round a few things out of generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum is a generous one, so both mean bountiful.

clue.text: Saved for new drapes

indicators.note: new suggests making something fresh, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Money kept aside to buy new curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone is to save them from harm.

clue.text: When marginal land experiences the least ups and downs

definitions.text: When marginal land experiences the least ups and downs

parts.words: When marginal land experiences the least ups and downs
parts.note: the land at the margin is the shore, and the ups and downs are the rise and fall of the sea

explanation.surface: Sounds like a time of calm for some fringe territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marginal land' is the shoreline; its 'ups and downs' are the tides, at their smallest twice a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide with the smallest range between high and low water, occurring at the moon's quarters.

clue.text: They're prepared to fight for a rise, possibly about a thousand

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part is placed around the other
possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Workers ready to strike for a pay rise of about a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns A RISE into ARIES, and 'about' puts it around M.
explanation.definitionFit: Large organised bodies of soldiers, trained and ready for battle.

clue.text: A burning issue!

parts.note: an issue is also an exit, and this is the way out of a building on fire

explanation.surface: A pressing topic of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means a way out, not a topic; 'burning' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stairs or a ladder for escaping a building when it is on fire.

clue.text: Purposeful muse

explanation.surface: An intentional thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means intended; as a verb it means to weigh things up or ponder.

clue.text: Calling outside right for a hammering

indicators.note: outside means one word is wrapped around another

parts.note: dubbing someone is calling them by a name

explanation.surface: Shouting angrily for a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts DUBBING around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy defeat or beating, as in a sporting thrashing.

clue.text: Bearing the transport charge

definitions.meaning: the fee paid for conveying goods

explanation.surface: How one carries oneself and the cost of freight.
explanation.definitionFit: It means deportment, and also the cost of conveying goods, as in carriage paid.

clue.text: She's responsible for maintaining order in retirement

definitions.text: She's responsible for maintaining order in retirement

parts.words: She's responsible for maintaining order in retirement
parts.note: order is a religious order and retirement is seclusion from the world

explanation.surface: A retired woman still keeping things tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' here is a religious community and 'retirement' is withdrawal into a convent, not old age.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun ranking next below an abbess, or heading a priory.

clue.text: Got up and phoned in-changed the order

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: reared means rose up, as a horse does
rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: Someone rose and called in to say plans had shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RANG inside REARED.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in a different sequence is to alter their order.

clue.text: Claim devastating note will cause ill-will

indicators.note: devastating suggests wrecking something, so the letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A damaging message breeds bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastating' rearranges CLAIM into MALIC, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or the desire to harm another.

clue.text: Think to take over

definitions.meaning: to suppose or take for granted
to take on a role or power, as in taking office

explanation.surface: Consider seizing control.
explanation.definitionFit: It means to suppose, and also to take on responsibility or control.

clue.text: Set on getting under canvas?

definitions.meaning: going into a tent, read whimsically as two words

explanation.surface: Keen on going camping.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN TENT, it describes being under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: It means resolved upon, and split in two it says inside a tent.

clue.text: Rail against the controversy in town

indicators.note: against means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: a bar is a rail or rod
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Protesting about a local dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: BARROW-in-Furness is a shipbuilding town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria, England.

clue.text: Asinine pair, popular though criminal

indicators.note: a pair means two of the same, so the piece is used twice

parts.note: asinine means like an ass, a donkey
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Two foolish people are well liked despite being crooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer, especially of a prominent person, is a criminal.

clue.text: Representations will be made if game is affected

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: A sport's portrayal changes if the game is tampered with.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures or likenesses that represent something.

clue.text: Work on hand

parts.note: a job waiting to be done, read literally as treatment of the hand

explanation.surface: A task currently pending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' looks like an idiom for pending, but it is literal: work done on a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic care of the hands and fingernails.

clue.text: This banded stone from Cologne is superb

indicators.note: from shows the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A German city boasts fine striped rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A metamorphic rock with light and dark layers or bands.

clue.text: Showing principle about people's housing

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men means people, with the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: Displaying a principle on housing for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TENET around MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into flats, a kind of housing.
